issues.description: Lost null guard / NPE regression: ours chains `.replace('\\','/')` directly onto `URIDecoder.decodeURIComponent(context.normalisedPath(), false)`, which returns null for null input (vertx-core 3.9.3 URIDecoder). The official fix restructured precisely for this — it binds `uriDecodedPath`, checks it for null, and only then calls replace(). With ours, a null normalisedPath() throws NPE at StaticHandlerImpl:131 (→ 500) instead of the intended `log.warn("Invalid path"); context.next();` (→ 404). Not reachable via RoutingContextImpl (it maps null request.path() to "/"), but handle() accepts the RoutingContext interface, so third-party/decorator implementations can hit it. Fix: hoist the decode into a local and move the existing null check above the replace, mirroring the official diff.

The code comment and both test comments attribute the flaw to "CVE-2023-24815 class path traversal", but the vulnerability under fix is CVE-2019-17640 (upstream commit b12f7c4c). Misleading provenance in a permanent code comment; the described mechanism is nonetheless correct.

Verification evidence is thin: only 2 regression tests ran. The behavior change makes any legitimate path containing an encoded literal backslash (valid on POSIX filesystems) unservable. This matches upstream intent ("handle all paths as UNIX paths") and is not a defect, but no broader StaticHandler suite result is presented to confirm no other assertions depend on the old behavior.

result.root_cause: StaticHandlerImpl fed the URI-decoded request path to HttpUtils.removeDots(), which per RFC 3986 §5.2.4 only recognises '/' as a segment separator, so a percent-encoded backslash ("/..%5c…" → "/..\…") passed dot-segment canonicalization untouched and reached the FileSystem sink with an intact ".." on platforms that honour '\' as a separator; a correct fix must fold '\' to '/' before canonicalization so the whole path is normalized as a UNIX path.
result.summary: Our patch is essentially the official fix: it folds '\' to '/' before HttpUtils.removeDots() on the exact line upstream changed, closing the backslash-separator bypass for the whole class (any encoding of '\' decodes to the same char and is normalized; double-encoding yields literal, non-separator chars), not just the POV payload. POV no longer reproduces, regressions pass, and the file set matches the official fix exactly. The one substantive divergence is that the official fix deliberately hoisted the decode into a local and moved the null check above the replace(); ours chains .replace() onto a value that URIDecoder.decodeURIComponent can return null for, converting a graceful "Invalid path"→next() into an NPE→500 — unreachable through RoutingContextImpl in-tree, but a real loss of a defensive guard on a public interface-typed API. Security-equivalent to the reference fix, marginally less robust on the null edge.
